info.name: Multi-Courier Integration Platform - Reviewer Journey
info.description: Import this collection after starting the NestJS service locally. Run requests top-to-bottom: it proves liveness, idempotent admission, replay safety, deferred MockCourier dispatch, tracking, cancellation, 1–100 batch admission, batch-status lookup, conflict handling, and strict validation. The default courier is MockCourier, so no external credentials are required.

request.description: Admits a normalized order. The local reference dispatcher returns 202 with a PENDING order; it does not call a courier during the HTTP request.
Re-submits exactly the same logical request. Idempotent admission returns the existing order rather than scheduling duplicate work.
Returns the normalized tracking view. The create response is PENDING, then the in-process MockCourier dispatch normally makes the next tracking view CREATED.
Cancels a pending order. Repeating cancellation is safe and returns the existing cancelled state.
Admits two orders concurrently. The API returns a batch resource immediately and continues courier dispatch after the HTTP response. Batch state is process-local in this reference mode.
Projects current item lifecycle state and preserves any admission error at item granularity. Run request 06 first so its test script stores batchId.

item.name: 08 - Reject a changed payload with the same order ID

request.description: Changes parcel weight while retaining the order ID. The API fails closed instead of accidentally creating a duplicate shipment.

  "orderId": "ORDER-POSTMAN-INVALID-1001",

request.description: Shows strict request whitelisting. Ambiguous fields are rejected instead of silently discarded.

exec: pm.test('validation error has a request ID', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error.requestId).to.be.a('string'));
